title: Yeah Hand (formerly Rebelia): an open source tendon-driven robotic and prosthetic hand
description:
Open source anthropomorphic hand, fully 3D-printable, usable as a robotic end effector and as an active prosthetic hand.

Five serial bus servomotors housed in the palm drive the fingers through antagonistic flexion and extension tendons wound in opposite directions on one spool per actuator. Ring and little fingers share one actuator through a sliding tendon loop that lets them adapt to the object. The thumb base is mounted directly on the output flange of the thumb rotation actuator. The ESP32-based firmware performs load-based tendon calibration at start-up, force-limited grasps and grasp presets controlled by a single closure value.

This record contains the complete design files (CAD, STL, electronic board, firmware) and documentation. It is published as open source hardware and as a public technical disclosure (prior art). First public disclosure on GitHub: 3 March 2025.

Hardware: CERN-OHL-S-2.0. Firmware: GPL-3.0-or-later. Documentation and images: CC-BY-SA-4.0. "Yeah Hand" is a registered EU trademark.
